Migrations are goose files in internal/db/migrations, numbered from the 'schema' sequence at merge, not at dispatch (owner, 2026-11-03: maximum parallel). A worker names its file 99999_<node-id>.sql; before merging, the dispatcher hands out the number with graph-node migration, renames the file, rebases on main and runs make generate. Workers never pick a number.

Generated sqlc packages are never hand-edited; make generate rewrites them. Nodes that write one package, or that each add a migration, may share a round: they merge one at a time, and each later one rebases on main, takes its migration number and runs make generate before it merges.

nodes.title: accept OAuth access tokens at /mcp
nodes.note: ADR-00034. Wires the OAuth token verifier into /mcp. Writes made with a token are logged in a new oauth_grant_writes table owned by internal/oauth, not in api_key_writes. Credential rows are deleted on revocation, and a bare INTEGER PRIMARY KEY reuses the newest freed id, so a credential id alone can name a later, unrelated credential. Each write row therefore also stores a snapshot that is never reused: for a grant, its client_id, owner email and created_at; for a key, the same fix applies to api_key_writes (its non-secret prefix, owner and created_at), in the same migration. Every lookup of a credential's writes (apikey.Store.Writes and its grant counterpart) matches on the snapshot as well as the id, and each log has a test that revokes the newest credential, issues a new one with the same id, and shows the old writes are not returned. May edit, as exceptions to append-only: the web.go r.Use line and the MCPVerifier default line, and the routes.go mountMCP line that builds the audit.

done.title: accept OAuth access tokens at /mcp
done.note: ADR-00034. Wires the OAuth token verifier into /mcp. Writes made with a token are logged in a new oauth_grant_writes table owned by internal/oauth, not in api_key_writes. Credential rows are deleted on revocation, and a bare INTEGER PRIMARY KEY reuses the newest freed id, so a credential id alone can name a later, unrelated credential. Each write row therefore also stores a snapshot that is never reused: for a grant, its client_id, owner email and created_at; for a key, the same fix applies to api_key_writes (its non-secret prefix, owner and created_at), in the same migration. Every lookup of a credential's writes (apikey.Store.Writes and its grant counterpart) matches on the snapshot as well as the id, and each log has a test that revokes the newest credential, issues a new one with the same id, and shows the old writes are not returned. May edit, as exceptions to append-only: the web.go r.Use line and the MCPVerifier default line, and the routes.go mountMCP line that builds the audit.
